title: Local maximum and minimum values
goal: Find flat spots on a 3D surface where $f_x = 0$ and $f_y = 0$ at the same time, then use the second-derivative test $D = f_{xx}f_{yy} - (f_{xy})^2$ to tell peaks, bowls, and mountain passes (saddles) apart.

beforeThis.skill: Algebra tip: when solving $f_x = 0$ and $f_y = 0$, factor instead of dividing by $x$ or $y$—if you divide by $x$, you throw away the solutions where $x = 0$!

links.label: Precalculus: Power functions and systems of equations

seeIt.title: Geometric Meaning of the Gradient Vector & Multivariable Optimization
seeIt.creator: Dr. Trefor Bazett
seeIt.watchFor: Shows why horizontal tangent planes ($f_x = 0$ and $f_y = 0$) locate peaks, valleys, and saddle points on a surface.

seeIt.title: Multi-variable Optimization & the Second Derivative Test
seeIt.creator: Dr. Trefor Bazett
seeIt.watchFor: Classifies a point where $f_x = f_y = 0$ with $D = f_{xx}f_{yy} - (f_{xy})^2$: positive $D$ is a peak or a bowl, negative $D$ is a saddle.

questions.asking: Find all values of the constant $c$ for which the discriminant $D = z_{xx}z_{yy} - (z_{xy})^2$ at $(0, 0)$ is strictly negative.
questions.statement: Use the Second Derivative Test to find all values of the constant $c$ for which the function $z = x^2 + cxy + y^2$ has a saddle point at $(0, 0)$.

questions.asking: Solve $f_x = 0$ and $f_y = 0$ to find all critical points of $f(x, y) = x^3 - y^3 - 2xy + 6$, and classify each as a local maximum, local minimum, or saddle point.
questions.statement:
Find and classify all critical points of the function

$$f(x, y) = x^3 - y^3 - 2xy + 6.$$

questions.asking: Find all solutions $(x, y)$ to $f_x = 0$ and $f_y = 0$, and classify each critical point as a local maximum, local minimum, or saddle point.
questions.statement: Find all critical points for $f(x, y) = x(x^2 + xy + y^2 - 9)$. Also find out which of these points give local maximum values for $f(x, y)$, which give local minimum values, and which give saddle points.
